subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Who wrote 'A Christmas Carol'?
questions.explain: Charles Dickens wrote the novella, first published in 1843.

questions.q: In which year was 'A Christmas Carol' first published?
questions.explain: The novella was first published on 19 December 1843.

questions.q: Into how many sections, called 'staves', is the novella divided?
questions.explain: Dickens divides the story into five staves, echoing the verses of a carol.

questions.q: Why does Dickens call the sections 'staves' rather than chapters?
options: A stave is a set of lines in music, keeping the 'carol' idea of a joyful song
It is the Victorian word for a legal document
It reflects the wooden staves used in workhouses
It refers to the five ghosts in the story
questions.explain: The musical term 'stave' reinforces the title's image of a Christmas carol.

questions.q: What is the name of Scrooge's dead business partner whose ghost first appears?
questions.explain: Jacob Marley's ghost visits Scrooge in Stave One to warn him.

questions.q: For how many years has Marley been dead at the start of the novella?
questions.explain: The opening establishes that Marley has been dead for seven years.

questions.q: In what order do the three spirits visit Scrooge?
questions.explain: The Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Yet to Come appear in that order.

questions.q: What is the name of Scrooge's poorly paid clerk?
questions.explain: Bob Cratchit is Scrooge's overworked and underpaid clerk.

questions.q: What does the character of Tiny Tim mainly represent in the novella?
options: The vulnerable, deserving poor and the value of compassion
The greed of the middle classes
questions.explain: Tiny Tim embodies innocent suffering that stirs Scrooge's compassion.

questions.q: What is the relationship between Scrooge and Fred?
questions.explain: Fred is Scrooge's cheerful nephew, the son of Scrooge's late sister Fan.

questions.q: Who was Belle in Scrooge's life?
options: His former fiancee who ended their engagement
questions.explain: Belle broke off her engagement to Scrooge as his love of money grew.

questions.q: The Ghost of Christmas Present reveals two children hidden beneath his robe. What do they symbolise?
questions.explain: The children Ignorance and Want warn of the consequences of neglecting the poor.

questions.q: Which of the following is the central theme traced across Scrooge's transformation?
questions.explain: Scrooge's journey from miser to generous man dramatises the theme of redemption.

questions.q: When asked to donate to the poor, Scrooge references prisons and which institutions, revealing his cold attitude?
questions.explain: Scrooge cites prisons and workhouses, echoing the harsh Poor Law provisions.

questions.q: The workhouses referenced in the novella were established under which piece of Victorian legislation?
options: The Poor Law Amendment Act of 1834
questions.explain: The 1834 Poor Law sent the destitute to harsh workhouses that Dickens criticised.

questions.q: Which aspect of Dickens's own childhood informed his sympathy for the poor?
options: His father was imprisoned for debt and Dickens worked in a blacking factory
He was raised in a wealthy aristocratic household
He trained as a doctor in London
He grew up on a country estate
questions.explain: Dickens's father was jailed for debt and the young Dickens laboured in a factory.

questions.q: What does Fezziwig, Scrooge's former employer, represent in contrast to Scrooge?
options: A generous, kind-hearted employer who values his workers
questions.explain: Fezziwig's warmth shows the humane employer Scrooge himself failed to be.

questions.q: A student argues the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come is the most frightening spirit. Which structural feature best supports this?
options: The ghost is silent and only points, forcing Scrooge to confront his own death
The ghost sings loudly throughout the stave
The ghost appears first in the novella
The ghost gives a long speech about redemption
questions.explain: The spirit's ominous silence heightens dread as Scrooge sees his lonely death.

questions.q: To show the redemptive power of Christmas at the end, which of Scrooge's actions in Stave Five is the strongest evidence?
options: He anonymously sends a large turkey to the Cratchits and raises Bob's salary
He locks himself away and counts his money
He refuses to attend Fred's dinner
questions.explain: His generosity to the Cratchits demonstrates his genuine, joyful transformation.

questions.q: A candidate wants to link the novella to Victorian attitudes to poverty. Which detail best illustrates the idea of the 'surplus population'?
options: Scrooge coldly suggests the poor should die to 'decrease the surplus population'
Fezziwig throws a lavish Christmas party
Tiny Tim says 'God bless us, every one'
questions.explain: Scrooge echoes Malthusian ideas that Dickens condemns as inhumane.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE English Literature (1ET0) specification; A Christmas Carol
